analysis.title: Reddit (RDDT): DAU Double Whammy
key_insights: Deutsche Bank keeps a Buy rating on Reddit but cuts its price target to $165 from $200 (-18%), based on 16x FY27 Adj EBITDA, down from 18x, to reflect near-term DAU challenges.
3Q26 users missed expectations. Global DAUq rose 12% y/y to 130.3mn, but US DAUq fell 2%, including a 4% drop in US logged-out users. Global weekly users grew 16% and US WAUq was essentially flat.

Search referrals weakened materially during 3Q and the pressure accelerated into 4Q. Reddit has lost about 1mn users each week in October. Extended through the end of 4Q, that implies a double-digit q/q DAU decline.

DB expects reported user growth to deteriorate through at least 2027. Causes are lower Search traffic (Google AI Mode is seen as a structural headwind) and Reddit's deliberate shift toward engagement over headline audience size.

User declines are not expected to hit revenue to the same degree. DB estimates logged-in users are about 40% of DAUs but roughly 80% of monetization, with engagement about 5x that of logged-out users, driven by time spent rather than higher CPMs.

Reddit is moving to an app-centric, logged-in ecosystem to improve personalization, ad signals, re-engagement and protection of its content corpus. The likely end state is a smaller but more engaged audience. Execution risk: an overly aggressive login wall could raise bounce rates and hurt Google rankings before owned channels can replace that traffic.

DB expects the Google data-licensing agreement to be renewed by the end of 1Q27, possibly with tighter content-usage limits, more prominent attribution or stronger referral mechanisms. DB sees Google's traffic changes as a broad structural shift and Reddit as collateral damage, not a targeted negotiating tactic. A renewal would remove an overhang and could be a significant catalyst.

3Q26 revenue beat the high end of guidance by 3%, below the recent average beat of 9%. Uneven, spiky September demand caused some booking slippage because the company could not deliver on a couple of days.

Ad performance was strong. Total ad revenue grew 54% against a 74% comp, click volume rose more than 50% and conversions more than tripled. Performance advertising is now over 60% of the business, and monetization is increasingly driven by ML, signals and measurement rather than higher ad load.

New ad products: Reddit Max adoption more than tripled q/q, shopping/app-install revenue grew more than 95%, video revenue more than doubled, and the shopping product can support up to 20mn SKUs. Search, shopping and video remain under-monetized surfaces.
3Q26 revenue grew 53% to $895mn versus DB's +49% estimate. ARPU grew 36% versus DB's 30% and DAU grew 12% versus DB's 14%. Adj. EBITDA was $402mn versus DB's $395mn.
DB cuts 4Q26 revenue to $1,027mn (+42% y/y) from $1,052mn, near the high end of the $1,000-1,030mn guide. It cuts 4Q26 Adj EBITDA to $499mn from $518mn, above the midpoint of the $490-510mn guide.
FY27 estimates are lowered. Revenue is now $4.3bn (+27% y/y, 6.9% below the prior estimate), Adj. EBITDA is $1.9bn versus $2.1bn before (44.4% margin versus 45.7%), and EPS is $7.50 versus $8.17.
DB cites revenue growth of +54% in 2026 and +27% in 2027, and about 15x consensus 2027 EPS as the valuation case. Near-term catalysts are a Google renewal or additional LLM licensing deals.

market_movers.rationale: Buy reiterated, target cut to $165 from $200 on a lower 16x FY27 Adj EBITDA multiple (was 18x) after weak DAU trends. The stock closed at $129.60 on 29 Oct 26.

sector_views.rationale: The report covers only Reddit. The one sector-level point is that Google's shift toward AI Mode is a structural headwind to search referral traffic.

earnings_insights: Reddit 3Q26 reported: revenue $895mn, +53% y/y, versus DB estimate +49%. This was a 3% beat of the high end of guidance, below the recent average beat of 9%.
Reddit 3Q26 reported: ARPU +36% versus DB estimate +30%. DAU +12% versus DB estimate +14%. Adj. EBITDA $402mn versus DB estimate $395mn.
Reddit 3Q26 reported: global DAUq 130.3mn (+12% y/y). US DAUq -2% y/y, US logged-out users -4%, global WAUq +16%, US WAUq essentially flat.
Reddit 3Q26 reported: total ad revenue +54% against a 74% comp. Click volume rose more than 50% and conversions more than tripled.
Reddit 4Q26 company guidance: revenue $1,000-1,030mn and Adj EBITDA $490-510mn. DB estimates (forecast) are revenue $1,027mn (+42% y/y, was $1,052mn) and Adj EBITDA $499mn (was $518mn).
DB FY27 estimates (forecast): revenue $4.3bn (+27% y/y), Adj. EBITDA $1.9bn (44.4% margin), EPS $7.50 (previously $8.17 EPS, $2.1bn Adj. EBITDA, 45.7% margin).
DB sees about 15x consensus 2027 EPS as attractive valuation, with revenue growth of +54% in 2026 and +27% in 2027.
risk_factors: User declines continue longer than expected. Reddit lost about 1mn users a week in October, and DB expects reported user growth to deteriorate through at least 2027.
Google AI Mode is a structural headwind to Search referral traffic, which Reddit depends on.
An overly aggressive login wall could raise bounce rates and weaken Google rankings, cutting off a top-of-funnel source before owned channels can replace it.
The Google and other data-licensing agreements expire in early 2027. Non-renewal, or renewal on less lucrative terms, could hurt investor sentiment.
International expansion may be slower than anticipated if Reddit does not succeed in non-English speaking markets.
Onboarding and Search functionality changes could disrupt growth if the transition does not go smoothly.

tension_points.bull_case: Logged-in users are about 40% of DAUs but roughly 80% of monetization, with about 5x the engagement of logged-out users. Moving users into the app should leave a smaller but better-monetized audience, and revenue is not expected to fall as much as users. Ad revenue grew 54% on a 74% comp.
tension_points.bear_case: US DAUq fell 2% and US logged-out users fell 4%. Reddit is losing about 1mn users a week in October, which would mean a double-digit q/q DAU decline if it continues through 4Q. Google AI Mode is a structural headwind, and the logged-in push adds friction.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An overly aggressive login wall raising bounce rates and weakening Google rankings, or non-renewal of the Google licensing agreement before it expires in early 2027.

theme_stances.key_argument: Google needs differentiated human content for its AI products, and Reddit gets high-margin licensing revenue, so both sides have strong incentives to renew.
theme_stances.evidence: we expect a deal by the end of 1Q27

theme_stances.key_argument: Shifting users to the app and logged-in experience gives Reddit more control over the experience and better signal, retention and monetization, though it will cost near-term DAU.
theme_stances.evidence: We view that as the right strategic move
